records.reason: Everything the artifact adds is a triggered survival rider — on being reduced to 0 HP you roll a flat check to stay at 1 HP, then can't heal for the encounter. This codebase deliberately keeps 'avoid being knocked out at 0 HP' as prose, not a modifier (see the note on mode 'item-crimson-godsblood-serum'), and no legal field expresses it. Its rapier statistics (d6 piercing, sword group, deadly d8, finesse, disarm) are already on the record; the printed +3 greater striking is the etchable rune lane (InventoryItem.runes), not an item field.
A mundane investigative tool whose entire content is permission to attempt a GM-rolled secret Thievery check against other creatures' DCs. No owner statistic changes.
Duplicate record of the same mundane kit; same reason — GM-rolled secret checks against other creatures, no owner statistic.
Plain ammunition. Its text is loading/crafting flavour plus a pasted copy of the generic Critical Specialization rules; it grants the owner nothing.
Plain ammunition, identical content to the 10-round row; grants the owner nothing.
A maintenance prerequisite — without it you can't do the daily upkeep that keeps a firearm from misfiring. It confers no bonus; the misfire rule itself is GM-run.

No printed numbers at all: 'distinctive effects ... to make onlookers marvel and even to gain an advantage in combat', plus a note that it exists for the Firework Technician archetype. There is nothing quantified to deliver.
A pet. The record itself says it cannot be combat trained or contribute to combat in any way.

The promise ('range increment of 20 feet' and the ranged trip / tethered / thrown / versatile P traits when thrown) is already delivered on the host weapon: items['combat-fishing-pole'] has range 20 and traits ranged-trip, tethered, thrown-20, versatile-p.
A mundane kit (pole, hooks, line, lures, net). Pure equipment description with no rule attached.

Text gives YOU (and allies) resistance 10 to damage from siege weapons while under the banner's aura, but the record carries no passiveEffects at all. The duplicate record major-flag-of-the-stronghold already ships exactly this shape, and flag-of-the-stronghold (base) ships value 5 — this row was simply missed.
Registered in core.runes.flaming as a weapon property rune with damage {dice:1,die:'d6',type:'fire',critPersistent:{dice:1,die:'d10'}} — exactly the printed text. Etched via InventoryItem.runes.

core.runes['flaming-greater'] carries damage 1d6 fire with critPersistent 2d10, matching the text. 'Ignores the target's fire resistance' is a target-side clause with nothing to put on the owner's sheet.

A relic gift (Aspect Fire), not a purchasable item — the GM grants it and its damage scales off the relic's level, which is GM-set. The activation is a spell attack resolved and gone in the same moment, and all the damage lands on the target.

A unique artifact that 'functions only for a specific tennin' — an NPC monster, not a player. Its content is Crafting/Repair downtime with a degree-of-success shift, which is a crafting-lane/GM adjudication with no legal field.

Every clause the text adds beyond the plain dagger statistics (already on the record: d4 piercing, knife group, agile, finesse, thrown-10, versatile-s) lands on the TARGET — the wounding rune's persistent bleed upgraded to 1d8, and the -2 status penalty to the victim's saves against disease. The printed +1 striking wounding is the etchable rune lane; core.runes.wounding exists.

Text: 'grant you a fist Strike that deals 1d6 damage, is in the brawling group, and has the magical and unarmed traits'. That is a new unarmed attack on the owner's sheet, and the record has no grantedStrikes — the Strikes card never learns about it. Damage type is not printed, so the fist default (bludgeoning) is used.

The unique text is conditional on wielding another unique artifact (Blood-Drinker) and then sets a flat printed attack modifier (+32) and a fly Speed for the ANIMATED weapon itself, not for the wielder. Its saber statistics and the dawnsilver material are already on the record; the printed +3 greater striking animated is the rune lane (core.runes has animated).
Mundane fire-starting gear; the text exists only to say it takes at least 3 actions and usually far longer. Nothing on the sheet.
Camping gear for zero-gravity planes. Capacity and anchoring are narrative; no owner statistic.
Same camping gear, one-person size. Narrative only.
Siege ammunition whose entire effect is on a ship's hull — it lodges in the wall and floods the hold. An object/vehicle effect resolved by the GM, nothing on the shooter's sheet.
An activated alarm tile placed on the ground: you set a weight threshold and it wails when tripped. It is battlefield furniture, not a modifier on the owner.
Mundane preservation tool for pressing plants. Pure flavour/downtime.

Text: 'The broom moves at a fly Speed of 20 feet' while you ride it, and the 2-action Lift Off activation raises that to 40 feet for up to 4 hours. That is a lasting, toggleable movement change with no record on the sheet. Modelled as an item mode (precedent: mode 'klingegeist' uses speeds.fly with a 'while ...' duration). The standing value is kept at 20 so simply owning the broom cannot over-grant the Lift Off speed.

mode.name: Riding the Flying Broomstick
mode.note: Guiding the broom with one hand gives a fly Speed of 20 feet; it can carry one passenger besides you. Activate—Lift Off (2 actions, concentrate, manipulate) toward a named destination on the same plane raises the fly Speed to 40 feet for up to 4 hours (about 16 miles) or until you Dismiss it — raise the speed to 40 by hand while that runs. Laden with more than 20 Bulk the broom takes a -10-foot penalty; above 30 Bulk it crashes. After the activation ends the broom can't be activated again for 1 hour.

records.reason: Mundane 10-foot ladder; the only rule is that folding or unfolding costs two Interact actions. Its two Bulk values are already the record's business.

The whole effect is an area attack against other creatures — three declining 15-foot cones of fire damage with a basic Reflex save. Nothing is added to the eater's own statistics, and per the audit rules a target-only effect gets no fix.
Same structure as Hotpops with poison damage in a 15-foot cone against other creatures — target-only, nothing on the owner's sheet.
Same structure as the other Follypops rows (the pasted text does not even reach the Sizzlers paragraph); the effect is an area attack on other creatures.
A relic gift (Aspect Soul). GM-granted, damage scales with character level, and the activation is a single burst of force damage against a target — resolved and gone.
A relic gift (Aspect Forge) that repairs a non-magical metal OBJECT once per day. Object repair is downtime/GM territory and touches no owner statistic.

A rare artifact whose two effects are (a) a constant Hidden Mind with a +32 counteract bonus — a narrative protection with no owner statistic and no field for a permanent spell effect — and (b) a save that OTHER creatures roll to forget you, which is entirely target-side.

A GM Core relic gift, not a purchasable item. The spell rank is 'half the item's level' and a relic's level is set by the GM as it grows, so there is no fixed rank to put in innateSpells; the chosen animal is agreed with the GM when the gift is gained.
A relic gift that only widens which polymorph spell the form of fury gift casts. Same reason: GM-granted, GM-scaled relic subsystem with no fixed rank.
A blank book that stores formulas. Storage capacity only — the formulas themselves are the crafting lane, and the text explicitly says no specific book is required.

core.runes.fortification exists (armor property, level 12, 2000 gp). The crit-to-normal-hit conversion is a flat check rolled at the table, and RuneDef has no field for the +1 Bulk / +1 Strength side effect — no legal lane exists for it, so the rune record is as complete as the schema allows.

core.runes['fortification-greater'] exists (armor property, level 18, 24000 gp). Same as the base rune: the crit negation is a table flat check, and the +1 Bulk / +1 Strength rider has no RuneDef field.

The three swappable gems ARE the flaming, frost and shock property runes, and all three ids exist in core.runes with their damage blocks; only one may be active at a time, which is precisely what the rune lane models (InventoryItem.runes holds one property rune, re-set when you Gem Twist). The +2 striking is the standard potency/striking lane. The 1d6 self-damage for twisting is resolved in the moment.
A pet; the record states it cannot be combat trained or contribute to combat in any way.

Consumable alchemical ammunition. It changes the damage type dealt to the TARGET, adds 2 cold splash, and can ice a 5-foot square that other creatures must save against. All of it is target/battlefield-side.
Consumable ammunition whose only effect is Slowed 1 (or 1 minute on a critical failure) imposed on the TARGET.
A pet; the record states it cannot be combat trained or contribute to combat in any way.
core.runes.frost carries damage {dice:1,die:'d6',type:'cold'}. The crit rider (target Slowed 1 on a failed save) is a condition imposed on the TARGET.
core.runes['frost-greater'] carries damage 1d6 cold. The crit slow and the 'ignores the target's cold resistance' clause are both target-side.

The bomb's own numbers are on the record: damage {dice:1,die:'d6',type:'cold'}, range 20, bomb group, splash trait. The 1 cold splash and the target's -5-foot status penalty to Speeds both land on the TARGET.

A unique adventure-path frame that holds the four fulcrum lenses. Everything it does depends on which lenses the GM has given you and on those lenses' own activations; the 'highest melee spell attack modifier of any lens' is a comparison between other records, not a standing owner bonus.
It destroys parchment placed inside and lets you re-read the last message destroyed. A narrative/utility trick with no owner statistic.
The only mechanical content is the folded Bulk, and the record's own bulk field (0.1 = light) is the folded value. The variant rows carry the two printed cases.
The folded Bulk is baked into the record: bulk 0.1 (light), i.e. the 1-Bulk book already reduced by 1. Folding/unfolding is a 1-minute Interact with nothing else on the sheet.
The folded Bulk is baked into the record: bulk 0 (negligible), i.e. the light-Bulk book already reduced by 1.
Consumable ammunition. The extra 2d12 and the can't-breathe rider on a critical hit are applied to the TARGET.
Consumable ammunition; identical target-side content — extra 2d12, can't breathe on a crit, severs an appendage if the persistent damage kills it.
The record carries no rules text at all (empty description), so the item promises nothing that could be delivered. It is a unique adventure artifact run by the GM.
A pet; the record states it cannot be combat trained or contribute to combat in any way.

Consumable ammunition. It borrows the ghost touch property for the shot and ignores cover on that one attack — resolved in the moment on a single Strike, and the flat check for concealment explicitly still applies. Nothing standing on the sheet.
The bomb's numbers are on the record: damage {dice:1,die:'d8',type:'vitality'}, range 20, bomb group, splash + vitality traits. The 1 vitality splash and the Enfeebled 1 rider apply to the TARGET.
The record carries no rules text at all (empty description) — there is nothing promised to deliver. Its 18 Bulk is already recorded.
core.runes['ghost-touch'] exists as a level 4 weapon property rune. Its whole effect is how the weapon interacts with incorporeal TARGETS — no owner statistic to move.

The artifact's numbers are already on the record: 5d8 force damage, 300-foot range, advanced firearm group, backstabber/concussive/fatal-d12/kickback traits, inubrix material. Both activations are momentary — one swaps the damage type for the triggering Strike, the other makes the next shot ignore cover — and the printed +4 major striking beast-bane greater impactful is the etchable rune lane.

Text: 'the implement is so ungainly that you are Clumsy 1 while wielding it' — a standing condition on the OWNER while the pole is wielded, plus the permission to Grapple with no free hand. Nothing on the record says so. Clumsy is carried in a mode note in this codebase rather than as modifiers (precedent: modes 'giants-stature', 'dire-form', 'item-hydra-mutagen' all note clumsy 1 instead of encoding it). The -2 circumstance penalty to the grabbed creature's unarmed Strikes is target-side and is left out.

mode.name: Wielding the Giant Catch Pole
mode.duration: while wielding the giant catch pole
mode.note: You are Clumsy 1 while wielding it (apply as a condition). The rope loop lets you Grapple without having a free hand, and the giant version can Grapple creatures up to your normal size limit rather than only Medium or smaller.
